newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania president backs oil terminal share law.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania president backs oil terminal share law.

text.p: Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas has agreed to sign a law paving the way for the government to cut its share in the planned Butinge oil terminal to a minority, Economy Minister Vincas Babilius said on Monday.
"The president said he will sign the law," Babilius told reporters after he and Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius met the President Brazauskas.
Brazauskas was set to approve a controversial law to cut the government's stake from over 90 to 34 percent in the delayed oil terminal as a way of speeding its completion and attracting investment.
Critics have said Butinge is too important a project for the government to own less than a majority stake.
Babilius said he now planned to meet Russian oil firms Lukoil and YUKOS to see if they were interested in taking part in the project.
Butinge has been surrounded by controversy and delay as funding and investment for the estimated $200 million terminal has been hard to come by.
The new law forbids the state from selling more than 33 percent to any single private investor.
"In the near future, I plan to meet with (Russia's) Lukoil and YUKOS to discuss investment possibilities," Babilius said.
Construction of the terminal, which will primarily be used for the export of Russian oil products, is scheduled for completion in late 1998.
A new share issue will soon be made to boost its share capital to 261 million litas from 72 million litas.
"The main problem is how to find investors for the issue," Vagnorius told journalists.
